articles.title: Will Jacks set to miss rest of England's white-ball tour of Australia after breaking hand in Melbourne T20I defeat
articles.summary: England batter Will Jacks has been ruled out of the T20 series against Australia after breaking his hand during his side's defeat in Melbourne; Jacks had been due to captain England for the first time in the fifth T20 on the Gold Coast
articles.body:
Jacks sustained the injury in the penultimate over of England's narrow defeat in the first T20I in Melbourne. He was forced to leave the field with blood streaming from his right hand after attempting a difficult caught-and-bowled chance off Ben Dwarshuis.

A fracture was subsequently confirmed, ruling him out of the remainder of the tour and forcing him to fly home while his team-mates continued to the Gold Coast. The injury also means he will miss the opportunity to captain England for the first time.

"Will Jacks has been ruled out of the remainder of the England men's white ball tour of Australia after breaking his hand in last night's T20 against Australia," the ECB confirmed in a statement on X.

"An update on plans to replace Jacks in the squad will be issued in due course."

With regular captain Harry Brook unavailable for the fifth and final T20I ahead of the Test series against South Africa, Jacks had been expected to lead England in Canberra on December 2.

That responsibility will now pass to Banton, who has been named Brook's deputy ahead of more experienced candidates. Phil Salt, who captained England against Australia in 2024 and Manchester Super Giants in The Hundred last season, was among the alternatives, alongside Sam Curran, who has led Punjab Kings in the IPL and Surrey in the Vitality Blast.

However, Banton has impressed the coaching staff since returning to the international fold, establishing himself as a quietly influential presence and making the most of opportunities created by injuries to Jacob Bethell and Jos Buttler.

Having already turned his temporary promotion to opener in the ODI side into a strong case for becoming England's first-choice option at next year's World Cup, the Somerset batter has now taken another step forward with his appointment as vice-captain.

Speaking at the end of the 50-over series, head coach Brendon McCullum namechecked the 28-year-old's growing status as someone who "exhibits the behaviours and understands the direction of travel you want from the team".

England are weighing up possible replacements for Jacks, having already called up Hampshire's Scott Currie to bolster numbers when Brook and Jordan Cox miss the fifth game.

As a spin bowling all-rounder with the ability to add power to the lower middle order, Rehan Ahmed would appear to be the closest to a like-for-like replacement.

Whether or not he is called up could offer an insight into his current standing in the pecking order. Since becoming England's youngest men's international in all three formats in 2022/23, he has struggled to establish a regular role. His leg-spin remains a work in progress, while his obvious batting talent has too often been undermined by carelessness.

The 22-year-old signed a one-year central contract in October only to be left out of the subsequent ODI tri-series in Pakistan and both squads for Australia.

Back with England Lions, Ahmed made a strong impression under new head coach Jonathan Trott during the recent tour of St Kitts to face West Indies A. He showcased his all-round ability in the second unofficial ODI, scoring an impressive 108 at number three before taking five for 60 with the ball.

He is due to rejoin the Lions for their upcoming tour of South Africa, but Jacks' withdrawal could open the door for Ahmed to return to the senior squad and reignite his international career.

articles.title: Matthew Hayden drops 'more smoke' remark on Sandpapergate, questions Australia's handling of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
articles.summary: Eight years after the infamous Sandpapergate scandal rocked Australian cricket, the controversy surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering incident refuses to
articles.body: Eight years after the infamous Sandpapergate scandal rocked Australian cricket, the controversy surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering incident refuses to die down. Fresh revelations from Cameron Bancroft and Usman Khawaja have once again brought questions of accountability and transparency into focus, with former Australia opener Matthew Hayden now calling for a fair and independent assessment of the entire episode.Hayden believes several questions surrounding the Cape Town Test against South Africa remain unanswered and has urged Cricket Australia to establish a transparent process that allows everyone involved to present their version of events."It's just undeniable that there is a lot more smoke to come out of this fire," Hayden said while speaking on JioStar's 'Sandpapergate: The Unsettled Debate'.The former opener stressed that Australian cricket needs to move beyond the original sanctions and establish whether the full extent of the incident was ever investigated. He also insisted that reconciliation and trust would remain difficult as long as doubts continued to surround the scandal.Hayden calls for independent inquiry, wants former players to have their sayHayden argued that Cricket Australia should take ownership of the process and consider an independent assessment to establish whether further investigation is warranted."Whether it's with Cricket Australia or an independent assessment process, I think we need to ask specific questions, and we need to identify if there are grounds for further inquiry, and then proceed with a clear scope and a fair process for everyone involved. There has to be some ownership over the process. Reconciliation is never going to be there for as long as there are question marks over integrity and trust," he said.The 54-year-old also emphasised that the process should not be restricted to current players, adding that those who were part of the 2018 South Africa tour and have since retired should also be given an opportunity to speak in an official capacity.He specifically mentioned David Warner and Usman Khawaja, along with other former players who have recently spoken about the controversy."It's unimaginable to think that the game can't actually get itself into a position where it at least understands a little bit further around the seriousness of this matter, and then come up with some sort of process that entitles not only the current players, but also the players that were involved in that series, who have now subsequently retired, David Warner and Usman Khawaja, to have their say in an official capacity, and the other three that have come out in support of it as well. I think as long as that gate remains open, there will be a distrust issue," Hayden added.What are the fresh Sandpapergate allegations?The debate has resurfaced following recent comments from Bancroft and Khawaja, who have questioned whether knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was limited to the three players who were initially punished.During the third Test against South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018, Bancroft was caught on television cameras using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball. The incident triggered one of the biggest crises in Australian cricket and resulted in suspensions for Bancroft, then captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner.In a recent column for The West Australian, Bancroft reportedly detailed conversations with members of the Australian bowling group about generating reverse swing. His account included discussions involving Pat Cummins and suggested that awareness of the plan may have extended beyond the three players who were sanctioned.Bancroft also claimed that his actions had been encouraged and celebrated within the team, adding another dimension to the long-running controversy.Khawaja has similarly raised questions about how much the wider Australian dressing room knew about the incident. Cummins, however, has strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as "utter nonsense".Hayden questions Cricket Australia's stance on the controversyHayden also questioned Cricket Australia's response to the latest revelations, arguing that the governing body must address the lingering doubts if it wants to restore public confidence.He acknowledged that the International Cricket Council (ICC) had strengthened its regulations following the incident, including expanding its rules and empowering on-field umpires to deal with ball tampering. However, he believes the broader questions surrounding the Australian team's conduct still need to be addressed."Until there is some further position on this from the authority, and that's Cricket Australia in this case, because the ICC have had their say. They've gone, 'Right, our rules have now expanded. We've got new policies. We've got empowerment of our umpires.' That's a really good thing that's come out of this, because we don't want to see unnecessary tampering of the ball. But Cricket Australia have taken a very definite position on this, and nothing is going to change public opinion," Hayden said.Drawing attention to the importance of a cricket ball to fast bowlers, Hayden questioned the suggestion that members of the bowling group could have been unaware of any plans to alter its condition."If you talk to a first-grade cricketer who's a fast bowler, and you tell him that he doesn't know what ball he's got in their hand, just like you heard Irfan say before, they will say, 'Mate, you are kidding. That'd be like someone tampering with my bat. And I know exactly every centimetre of that bat. It's just undeniable that there is a lot more smoke to come out of this fire," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Jasprit Bumrah produced a remarkable double strike against New Zealand captain Tom Latham, dismissing him for a duck in the first over of both innings in
articles.body: Jasprit Bumrah produced a remarkable double strike against New Zealand captain Tom Latham, dismissing him for a duck in the first over of both innings in the opening Test.Bumrah became only the third Indian bowler to achieve the feat in a Test match, joining former India pacers S Sreesanth and Zaheer Khan.The Indian speedster first struck in New Zealand's opening innings, bowling Latham for a two-ball duck. The left-handed batter shouldered arms to a delivery pitched around the fourth-stump line, expecting it to move away, but Bumrah got the ball to nip back sharply and crash into the off-stump.Bumrah repeated the trick in New Zealand's second innings, removing Latham for another duck, this time off the second ball. The New Zealand skipper attempted a tentative push at a delivery that angled away from him, only to edge it behind to wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant.Latham's two dismissals meant he registered a pair, while Bumrah continued his impressive record against the New Zealand captain.Before Bumrah, Sreesanth and Zaheer Khan had achieved the distinction of taking a wicket in the first over of both innings of a Test.Sreesanth dismissed West Indies opener Chris Gayle twice in the first over at Kingston in 2006, while Zaheer achieved the feat against Bangladesh in Mirpur in 2007, dismissing Javed Omar off the very first ball of both innings.Bumrah's double strike came as India strengthened its grip on the Test after posting a mammoth 720/9 declared in its first innings, the highest total by any team in a Test in New Zealand.India secured a 352-run first-innings lead after bowling New Zealand out for 368. KL Rahul top-scored with 136, while Rishabh Pant smashed 128 off 153 balls. Yashasvi Jaiswal (85), Devdutt Padikkal (80), Shubman Gill (98) and Dhruv Jurel (78) also made significant contributions.New Zealand were 119/2 at stumps on the fourth day, with Devon Conway unbeaten on 59 and Rachin Ravindra on 27, but still trailing by 233 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Big blow for England! Will Jacks ruled out of Australia T20I series after breaking hand in first match
articles.summary: Melbourne: England have suffered a major setback on their Australia tour, with all-rounder Will Jacks ruled out of the remainder of the white-ball series
articles.body: Melbourne: England have suffered a major setback on their Australia tour, with all-rounder Will Jacks ruled out of the remainder of the white-ball series after breaking his hand during the opening T20I against Australia in Melbourne on Saturday (November 21).The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) confirmed that Jacks would take no further part in the tour after medical assessments revealed a fracture in his right hand. The governing body added that an update on his replacement would be announced in due course.Jacks sustained the injury while bowling in England's three-wicket defeat against Australia at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. The all-rounder was attempting a return catch in his follow-through when Ben Dwarshuis struck the ball back towards him, hitting his bowling hand.The incident occurred during Jacks' third over, with the visuals suggesting a possible split webbing as he immediately appeared to be in considerable pain. The England physio attended to him before the all-rounder was forced to leave the field for further medical attention.Will Jacks injury comes at crucial stage of Australia chaseJacks' injury came at a decisive stage of Australia's run chase, with the hosts needing just 12 runs from the final eight deliveries.After the incident, Henry Crocombe completed the final two deliveries of Jacks' over. England subsequently handed the responsibility of bowling the final over to Sam Curran, who was tasked with defending 11 runs.However, Jack Edwards struck a boundary off the penultimate delivery to seal a thrilling three-wicket victory for Australia with one ball remaining. The result also saw Australia complete their highest successful men's T20I chase against England, reaching the target of 188 to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.Australia vs England: Remaining T20I scheduleWith Jacks unavailable, England will now have to reassess their combination for the remaining four matches as they look to bounce back and level the series. The second T20I will be played at Carrara on November 24, before the teams travel to Brisbane for the third match on November 27.The fourth T20I is scheduled to take place at the Sydney Cricket Ground on November 29, while the series will conclude with the fifth match at Manuka Oval in Canberra on December 2.Remaining fixtures:2nd T20I – November 24, Carrara, Gold Coast3rd T20I – November 27, The Gabba, Brisbane4th T20I – November 29, Sydney Cricket Ground, Sydney5th T20I – December 2, Manuka Oval, CanberraGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Rishabh Pant continued to rewrite the record books with his attacking batting, climbing to second place on the list of most sixes in Test cricket during India's first innings against New Zealand in the opening Test.The India wicketkeeper-batter now has 108 sixes in the longest format, moving past former New Zealand captain Brendon McCullum, who finished his Test career with 107 sixes. His innings featured six sixes and 10 boundaries as he took the attack to the New Zealand bowlers and helped India post a mammoth 720/9 declared.The 28-year-old was particularly aggressive against Glenn Phillips, completing his century with a straight six before sending another delivery over extra cover. Earlier, he had also deposited Kyle Jamieson over long-on with a powerful hit that landed in the adjacent car park.Pant's latest achievement further underlined his reputation as one of the most destructive batters in Test cricket. articles.body: The much-anticipated India A versus Pakistan A clash in the Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 had no shortage of intensity, with fast bowler Harshit Rana adding fuel to the contest through an animated send-off to Pakistan opener Shamyl Hussain on Sunday.With emotions running high between the arch-rivals, Rana was involved in a few heated exchanges with Pakistan's opening batters during his bowling spell. The Indian pacer, known for his aggressive approach, did not shy away from expressing himself as he tried to break the opposition's opening partnership.Pakistan got off to a flying start after opting to bat first, with Shamyl Hussain and Maaz Sadaqat putting India's bowling attack under pressure. articles.title: ‘Booed and cheered’: Usman Khawaja gets mixed reception at T20 Gold Cup in Queensland, shares the field with Darren Lehmann
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja received a mixed reception of boos and cheers at the T20 Gold Clash in Queensland while sharing the field with ex-coach Darren Lehmann.
articles.body:
Australia 's Usman Khawaja drew a split reaction from the crowd in Cairns on Sunday.

He played alongside Darren Lehmann, who has openly rejected his Sandpapergate claims about 2018.

Small details at the anthem and in the middle added to the awkward atmosphere.

Sandpapergate fallout: Usman Khawaja booed and cheered in Queensland return

Cheers and jeers rang out together in Cairns on Sunday as Usman Khawaja stepped into the spotlight at the T20 Gold Clash.

It was a reception that summed up how divided opinion has become around the former Test opener, as some made their displeasure known the moment he appeared, while others backed him loudly, and the noise never settled into one clear verdict.

It was his first public outing in his home state of Queensland since the release of his autobiography, Sabr , which reopened the argument over the 2018 ball-tampering affair. In the book, Khawaja claimed that the Australian team knew all about the plan to tamper with the ball in Cape Town, a statement that has kept him in the headlines ever since.

The occasion saw Darren Lehmann, who was Australia's Test coach when the scandal broke, named in the same side. Lehmann has firmly denied the fresh allegations, so the two men being on the same team at a light-hearted event made for an uncomfortable picture.

What happened during the match - Highlights as Team Footy beats Team Cricket

This was the first time the pair, Lehmann and Khawaja, had been seen together in public since Khawaja revived one of the most controversial chapters in Australian sport.

Lehmann had missed the players' function and the meet-and-greet because he was working for the media at the Saturday night T20 international in Melbourne, so the two did not get much time to talk beforehand.

During the national anthem, the distance between them was obvious. Team Cricket captain Mike Hussey and Matthew Hayden stood in between Khawaja and Lehmann, and it looked like a deliberate piece of arrangement.

Hayden, who stood close to Khawaja at the anthem, has been among the sharpest critics. Speaking on For The Love Of Cricket last week, he took aim at the tone of Khawaja's public comments and the way he tells the story.

Hayden said that Khawaja's Instagram commentary contains "a lot of 'me and I'" and nothing like "us".

He then argued that the book will not be remembered well, adding that it is "a story that will be read and not revered."

Nonetheless, his innings gave the crowd plenty to react to, as he smashed 35 off only 18 balls before holing out to the bowling of Kate McCarthy, a former AFLW player and commentator.

His walk back drew a fresh round of boos, cheers and applause. The 39-year-old, now 39 years of age, appeared to lift his bat slightly towards the stands, a small gesture that acknowledged the noise without answering it.

In the end, Team Footy won the game by five wickets.

Usman Khawaja's Cairns reception shows the Sandpapergate debate is far from over

The noise in Cairns told a story that no statement could. A crowd that boos and cheers the same man in the same minute is a crowd that has not decided what it thinks, and that uncertainty is probably the most honest reaction available.

Khawaja is entitled to tell his own version of 2018, yet he has to accept that a version naming an entire team will face stiff resistance, especially when Cummins, Hazlewood, Starc and Lehmann have all disagreed publicly.

The most telling image was not the dismissal or the raised bat but the order of players at the anthem. Hussey and Hayden standing between two men who share a sport and a past showed how raw the mutual feelings remain, and it is hard to imagine a gentler way of handling it.

articles.title: India rewrite Test history in New Zealand! Records broken as Shubman Gill and Co. pile up 720
articles.summary: India produced a batting masterclass on Day 4 of the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington, piling up 720/9 declared to register their
articles.body: India produced a batting masterclass on Day 4 of the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington, piling up 720/9 declared to register their third-highest total in Test cricket and their highest-ever score in an overseas Test innings.Rishabh Pant led the charge with a blistering 128 off 153 balls, while KL Rahul (136), Yashasvi Jaiswal (85), Devdutt Padikkal (80), Shubman Gill (98) and Dhruv Jurel (78) also made significant contributions.India's monumental total came with a host of records, including becoming the first team in Test history to register seven consecutive 50-plus partnerships in an innings.New Zealand were 119/2 at stumps, still trailing by 233 runs after Devon Conway's unbeaten 59 offered some resistance.Here are the key statistics and records from Day 4 of the opening Test:1. India breach 700 for the fifth time in Test cricketIndia's 720/9 declared is their third-highest total in Test cricket and their highest-ever score in an away Test innings.It is also the highest total by any team against New Zealand in Test cricket, surpassing the West Indies' 660/5 declared at the same Wellington venue in 1995.India's score is also the highest by any team on New Zealand soil, bettering the hosts' 715/6 declared against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.India's 700-plus totals in Test cricket:ScoreOpponentVenueYear759/7dEnglandChennai2016726/9dSri LankaMumbai2009720/9dNew ZealandWellington2026707Sri LankaColombo (SSC)2010705/7dAustraliaSydney2004India have now registered five 700-plus totals in Test cricket, a tally bettered only by Sri Lanka, who have seven. England, Australia and the West Indies have four each, while Pakistan have two and New Zealand one.2. India's seven successive 50-plus partnerships create Test historyFor the first time in Test cricket, a team recorded 50-plus partnerships for each of the first seven wickets in an innings.India's seven successive stands were:130 runs for the first wicket165 runs for the second wicket91 runs for the third wicket100 runs for the fourth wicket68 runs for the fifth wicket75 runs for the sixth wicket54 runs for the seventh wicketIndia's seven 50-plus partnerships are also the joint second-most in a Test innings, alongside Australia's seven against England in Sydney during the 2025-26 Ashes.The record belongs to India, who registered eight such partnerships against England at The Oval in 2007.3. Top five Indian batters score 80-plusIndia achieved a rare batting feat as each of their top five batters scored at least 80 runs in the innings.This was only the second instance of a team having its top five batters score 80 or more in a Test innings.Interestingly, the previous instance also came against New Zealand, when Pakistan recorded 566/3 declared at Abu Dhabi in 2014.4. India almost match their entire 2020 New Zealand tour tally in one inningsIndia's 720-run effort was particularly remarkable considering their previous Test tour of New Zealand in 2020.India had managed a combined 722 runs across four innings during that tour, scoring 165 and 191 in Wellington before making 242 and 124 in Christchurch.They came within touching distance of surpassing that entire tally in a single innings this time around.5. India register their highest-ever Test score against New ZealandIndia's previous highest total against New Zealand in Test cricket was 583/7 declared in Ahmedabad in 1999.Their 720/9 declared in Wellington comfortably surpassed that mark.It was also only India's second 500-plus total in New Zealand, following their 520 all out at Hamilton in 2009.6. Rishabh Pant scores his ninth Test centuryPant struck 128 off 153 deliveries to register his ninth Test century.It was also his fourth Test hundred since returning to the format in 2024.The wicketkeeper-batter became the first Asian wicketkeeper and the sixth Indian batter to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries: South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.He also moved to second place on the list of most sixes in Test cricket with 108, going past Brendon McCullum's 107. Only England's Ben Stokes, with 138, is ahead of him.7. New Zealand face a daunting task after Bumrah's early strikeIndia's massive first-innings total gave them a 352-run lead after New Zealand were bowled out for 368.Jasprit Bumrah struck early in the second innings, dismissing New Zealand captain Tom Latham for a duck to hand him a pair in the match.Prasidh Krishna later removed Henry Nicholls for 31, with Dhruv Jurel taking an excellent catch at short leg.Devon Conway remained unbeaten on 59, while Rachin Ravindra was 27 not out as New Zealand reached 119/2 at stumps.The hosts still trailed by 233 runs heading into the final day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Four wickets in four balls! Debutant creates history as Jamshed Alam steals the show in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy
articles.summary: Vidarbha pulled off a thrilling chase against Gujarat in a rain-shortened 13-over contest, while several teams produced dominant performances in the Syed
articles.body: Vidarbha pulled off a thrilling chase against Gujarat in a rain-shortened 13-over contest, while several teams produced dominant performances in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy matches on Sunday.Openers Atharva Taide and Danish Malewar provided the platform for Vidarbha's pursuit of 129. Despite a late wobble, they managed to get over the line off the penultimate delivery. Earlier, Gujarat had made a flying start through Aarya Desai, who scored 41 off 23 balls, and Urvil Patel, who smashed 35 off 16. However, Parth Rekhade's three-wicket haul triggered a slowdown and restricted Gujarat to below 130.Himachal Pradesh captain Pukhraj Mann led from the front with a blistering 61 off 31 deliveries, helping his side post 183 against Tripura. He outscored opposition skipper Manisankar Murasingh, who claimed four wickets. Rohit Kumar and Aryaman Dhaliwal then picked up three wickets apiece to put Tripura on the back foot. Despite Lakshay Thareja's fighting fifty at No.5, Tripura could manage only 151, falling 32 runs short.Kunal Singh Rathore stole the show with an unbeaten century as Rajasthan registered a comprehensive 67-run victory over Mizoram. Contributions from Kartik Sharma, Mukul Choudhary and Mahipal Lomror provided further impetus to Rajasthan's innings as they posted 224/5. Mizoram attempted to fight back through Chinmay Sutar, who continued his impressive run with a 25-ball 48, but the target remained well beyond their reach.Debutant Jamshed Alam made an extraordinary entry into T20 cricket, taking four wickets in four consecutive deliveries for Railways against Saurashtra. He eventually finished with figures of 5/38, with five Saurashtra batters dismissed for ducks. Harvansh Pangalia offered resistance with an 80, but received little support as Railways defended their total of 183. Late contributions from Krains Fuletra, who struck 36 off 23 balls, and Under-19 star Mohit Ulva, who made 22 off 15, helped Saurashtra reduce the margin of defeat.Mumbai bounced back from a disappointing start to cruise to a nine-wicket win over Chhattisgarh. Angkrish Raghuvanshi, who had registered a duck in his previous outing, remained unbeaten on 84 to guide the chase of 160. Hardik Tamore chipped in with 41, while Musheer Khan contributed 29. Earlier, Shivam Dube led Mumbai's bowling effort with 3/21. Chhattisgarh's 17-year-old prospect Vikalp Tiwari provided a spark with an eight-boundary 41 off just 18 balls, but the rest of the top order failed to build on his effort.Kerala put up an imposing 204/4 against Puducherry, with Mohammed Azharuddin and Rohan Kunnummal registering half-centuries after Sanju Samson's quick 17 off nine deliveries. Vishnu Vinod also made a brisk contribution to lift the total. MD Nidheesh then dismantled Puducherry's top order. Prasad Pawar's 67, along with useful knocks from Ankit Sharma (45) and Sagar Trivedi (34), kept them in the contest, but Kerala eventually secured an 18-run victory.Delhi's top order delivered a commanding batting display, with Priyansh Arya continuing his rich vein of form alongside Yash Dhull and Nitish Rana to take the side to 232/6. However, Tejasvi Dahiya produced the standout innings, hammering 95 off just 36 balls at No.4. Haryana struggled to keep pace with the required rate during their reply. Suyash Sharma picked up three wickets, while Mayank Yadav claimed two to seal a comfortable win for Delhi.Hyderabad registered a convincing victory over Uttarakhand after veteran left-arm pacer Chama Milind claimed four wickets to bowl them out for 146. New-ball partner Chinntla Readdi supported him with three scalps. Uttarakhand suffered two significant batting collapses, losing their last six wickets for just 22 runs. Hyderabad's chase revolved around Kodimela Himateja, whose 77 proved decisive despite wickets falling at the other end. His effort helped Hyderabad complete the chase in the 16th over.Jitesh Sharma produced a match-winning display with the bat as Baroda chased down Bengal's 173-run target. Jitesh smashed 54 off 29 balls, overshadowing Abhimanyu Easwaran's 78 off 46 for Bengal. Krunal Pandya and Safvan Patel picked up identical figures of 2/33, striking at different stages to restrict Bengal. Shashwat Rawat then laid the foundation of Baroda's chase with a 35-ball 51 before Jitesh's aggressive knock carried them home.Madhya Pradesh held their nerve to edge Maharashtra by five runs in a closely fought contest. Maharashtra came close to pulling off the chase on the back of a late fifty from Arshin Kulkarni, but two run-outs in the final two deliveries ended their hopes. Openers Prithvi Shaw and Sahil Parakh had earlier struck half-centuries, while Kumar Kartikeya's 2/33 helped MP apply the brakes in the middle overs. MP had posted 208/9, with Harsh Gawali and Akshat Raghuwanshi scoring fifties and Rajat Patidar adding a quick 31 off 18 balls.Karnataka endured a difficult outing with the bat, getting bowled out for just 95 against Chandigarh. Hardik Chowdhry and Bhagmender Lather picked up three wickets each to leave Karnataka struggling throughout their innings. Karun Nair was their highest scorer with 25 off 22 deliveries. Chandigarh captain Shivam Bhambri then led the chase with a half-century as his side wrapped up the target in 14 overs.Abdul Samad produced a stunning late assault to power Jammu and Kashmir to a remarkable chase against Punjab. Samad remained unbeaten on 64 off 27 balls, smashing seven sixes, while No.7 Lone Muzaffar provided crucial support with a six off the penultimate delivery. Opener Qamran Iqbal had earlier set the platform with a half-century, although Harpreet Brar's spell slowed down the scoring. Punjab had posted 195, built around Vivaan Malhotra's 85 off 59 balls and a half-century from Ramandeep Singh towards the end. However, Samad's explosive finish ensured Jammu and Kashmir crossed the line.All three Plate matches in Sovima, Nagaland, were abandoned due to rain. articles.summary: Former New Zealand captain Kane Williamson has revealed that a conversation with Virat Kohli played an important role in helping him reach the decision to
articles.body: Former New Zealand captain Kane Williamson has revealed that a conversation with Virat Kohli played an important role in helping him reach the decision to retire from international cricket in June, describing the interaction as being like ‘looking in the mirror’.Williamson brought the curtain down on his 16-year international career, ending his journey as New Zealand's highest run-scorer in Test cricket with 9,515 runs and a national-record 33 centuries.Speaking to former England captain Nasser Hussain on the latest episode of The ICC Review, Williamson explained why Kohli was among the people he wanted to speak to before making the significant career decision. The Indian batter had himself recently experienced stepping away from international cricket in two formats, making him someone who could relate to Williamson's situation.“I have a great relationship with Virat, and we’ve chatted many times over the years and obviously played against each other for a long time," Williamson said.“And I suppose off the back of that and our relationship it just felt right to chat to someone that you knew had the very experience of stepping away from the game not all that long ago and fully understood where you’re at."The relationship between the two batting greats goes back to their Under-19 days. They subsequently became captains of India and New Zealand and, alongside Steve Smith and Joe Root, were part of cricket's celebrated 'Fab Four'.Their connection, Williamson explained, extended beyond their battles on the field. Having experienced the demands of international cricket, leadership responsibilities and starting families during their careers, the two shared a perspective that few others could fully understand.Williamson said the exchange helped him look at his own circumstances more clearly and reinforced his feeling that the time had come to move on.“It’s been quite unique and our sort of story together, from under-19s to international cricket and even having a family and then leading our country and sort of being quite close throughout that journey along the way whilst competing against each other on numerous occasions. But it was just sort of like looking in the mirror, sharing those thoughts, fully understanding each other, and then getting off that call and knowing that it was time."While Williamson has stepped away from international cricket, Kohli remains active in the ODI format and has his sights set on representing India at the 2027 World Cup.The conversation also highlighted the challenges that come with being an international cricketer across formats. Constant travel, limited time with family, the demands of national and franchise commitments and the responsibility of leading teams make life at the highest level particularly demanding.For players who have spent years navigating that schedule, deciding when to walk away can be as difficult as the cricket itself. Williamson found clarity through a conversation with a fellow competitor who understood those demands first-hand.Kohli, meanwhile, could face similar career questions after next year's World Cup, depending on how things unfold.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A were bowled out for 265 in 49.1 overs while chasing Pakistan A’s 314, despite a magnificent ton from captain Tilak Varma and a spirited half-century from Shahbaz Ahmed in their ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 Group B clash on Sunday in Doha, Qatar.Varma stood tall amid a dramatic batting collapse, scoring 100 off 149 balls, with seven fours and a six. He anchored the innings after India A lost Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (11), Ayush Badoni (0) and Abhishek Sharma (70) inside the first 16 overs.Abhishek had provided a blistering start to the chase, smashing six fours and six sixes in his 42-ball knock before Hasan Nawaz ended his assault at 93/3.Pakistan A’s spinners and disciplined bowling then tightened their grip. Sufyan Moqim bowled Kumar Kushagra for 2, while Nawaz removed Rinku Singh (6) and Suryansh Shedge (3) to leave India A reeling at 129/6.With the required rate climbing and wickets falling, Varma found an able partner in Shahbaz Ahmed. The pair produced a superb seventh-wicket stand of 112 runs, briefly reviving India A’s hopes.Shahbaz counterattacked with 56 off 49 balls, striking four sixes and a boundary, while Varma continued to accumulate runs at the other end.Their partnership ended when Ali Raza dismissed Shahbaz in the 44th over, caught by Hasan Nawaz. Raza then removed Vipraj Nigam for a duck, while Mohammad Imran Randhawa dismissed Harshit Rana, leaving India A at 244/9.Varma eventually fell for a valiant 100 in the 50th over, caught by Rohail Nazir off Ahmed Daniyal, bringing the innings to a close at 265.Earlier, Pakistan A had posted 313 all out in 49.2 overs, built around Hasan Nawaz’s 79 and Farhan Yousaf’s 56. Nawaz also proved decisive with the ball, finishing with three wickets for 45 runs. Ali Raza claimed three for 56, while Randhawa took two wickets.Despite Varma’s remarkable resistance and Shahbaz’s late counterattack, India A fell 48 runs short of the target. Pakistan A’s collective bowling effort and crucial middle-order contributions proved decisive in a compelling contest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
